record.original_question: Is mathematics quasi-empirical, and more specifically, should mathematics be practiced more like physics?

evidence.quote: Is mathematics quasi-empirical? In other words, should mathematics be done more like physics is done? (I believe the answer to both questions is ‘Yes.’) (G. J. Chaitin)

artifact.self_contained_problem: A mathematical theory is called quasi-empirical if, in addition to (or in place of) deductive proof from fixed axioms, new axioms and principles are accepted on the basis of empirical-style evidence such as numerical experiments, heuristic plausibility, fruitfulness of consequences, agreement with computer-assisted experiments, or coherence with already-accepted results — much as physical theories are justified by experimental evidence rather than by derivation from first principles. Question: Is mathematics quasi-empirical in this sense? More specifically, should the practice of mathematics adopt a methodology analogous to that of physics, in which conjectures supported by sufficiently strong empirical or computational evidence are accepted as working axioms (for example, adopting statements such as the Riemann Hypothesis, P ≠ NP, or suitable large-cardinal axioms as new axioms on the basis of empirical support), rather than restricting acceptance to statements that have been formally proved from a fixed axiomatic foundation? Provide a justified answer, including criteria under which empirical evidence in mathematics would warrant the adoption of new axioms.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing methodological/philosophical question in the foundations of mathematics, repeatedly raised in works on quasi-empiricism (Lakatos, Putnam, Chaitin) and in discussions of accepting unproved hypotheses (e.g., RH, large cardinals) as axioms. There is no consensus answer; the question remains an open philosophical/methodological problem rather than a settled mathematical theorem.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-empiricism in mathematics — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Quasi-empiricism in mathematics is a movement... arguing that mathematical practice has empirical features and remains a subject of ongoing philosophical debate.
status_evidence.claim: The status of mathematics as quasi-empirical is an unresolved philosophical/methodological question.
